newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes keep low profile, imports thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes keep low profile, imports thin.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes remained elusive amid a tightly shut arbitrage with refiners continuing to source cheaper domestic supplies, traders said Monday.
A sharp rally in outright prices, but in tandem with firm Brent, kept the West Texas Intermediate to Brent Nov spread at a low 80 cents, leaving imports too pricey for refiners.
"No Brents or West African spot cargoes are being talked at all because it's too expensive," a Midwest trader said.
Brent was notionally pegged at Dec WTI plus 60 cents cif for second-half November, but with the fate of one ULCC fixed from Sullom Voe to the U.S. on subjects unclear.
Brent was rumored done in the later U.S. session at Nov Brent futures minus five cents fob for Oct 29-31, compared with an earlier Oct 29-31 trade at Nov Brent minus 10 cents.
A third Brent was heard done for late October into Canada, but this could not be verified.
Within the region, Latin American sellers offered several cargoes but at mostly strong levels except for Oriente.
The grade, seen diminishing in quality and amply supplied was offered into the U.S. at WTI minus $2.35 cif.
Ecopetrol offered three cargoes of South Blend, one cargo from November through January, in a sale tender.
Escalante for Nov 23-24 was also offered by YPF, following a recent sale at WTI minus $3.12 a barrel fob.
In the U.S. after market, Brent intermonth Nov/Dec paper traded once at 40 cents in subdued activity, within the range seen earlier in London.
Nov Brent was notionally assessed at $24.77-80 cents, a shade off London's IPE settlement.
